mbm-1876.clue: The price tag was inside the bell.
mbm-1876.quote: A shopkeeper let me try every bicycle bell on his counter. I chose the hoarse little blue one. Now my mother knows I'm at her gate before I even get off the bike.

mbm-1877.clue: The little mechanic needs room for a sandwich.
mbm-1877.quote: I made a lunchbox for my robot pilot and packed a tiny loaf and a pickle. I need tweezers to get the pickle out. The lid closes with a very satisfying click.

mbm-1878.clue: I keep a library card tucked into the score.
mbm-1878.quote: We practice our quartet in the library after closing. The librarian comes round listening for the quietest note. I swear our librarian can shush a song into tune.

mbm-1879.clue: My plaid sleeves have a second job.
mbm-1879.quote: We watch the late movie under one blanket. At sad endings my dad needs a tissue and my niece needs another. I keep a spare up my plaid sleeve.

mbm-1880.clue: This leather notebook shuts with a leaf.
mbm-1880.quote: I couldn't find a brass clasp I liked, so I cut one from stiff brown leather in the shape of a curled leaf. My sister keeps a pressed one beside each drawing inside.

mbm-1881.clue: I listen for the scrape of the third chair.
mbm-1881.quote: In our tiny rehearsal room the back corner of the waltz passes three café chairs. We used to bump the third one. Last Tuesday we slid past so cleanly the pianist stopped to cheer.

mbm-1882.clue: That scribble is a feather, honestly.
mbm-1882.quote: I tried to draw the tail of a wagtail while it was still wagging. My niece thought I'd drawn a metronome and set it beside the piano. Our duet keeps wonderfully irregular time.

mbm-1883.clue: I know one movie from a shoebox.
mbm-1883.quote: When our local theater closed, I helped pack the lobby letters. We kept the W from the first film I saw there. It stands on my shelf like two tiny empty seats.

mbm-1884.clue: The edge of the frame has a thumbprint.
mbm-1884.quote: My little brother took our picture with the sea behind us. His thumb left a bright red moon in the corner, just above the sun. It's the only photo everyone asked me to enlarge.

mbm-1885.quote: Our domino club meets in a bakery. I made the baker a set with the dots iced onto biscuits. He put the double-four on my saucer and the game was over at the first bite.

mbm-1886.clue: My chess partner owes me half a scarf.
mbm-1886.quote: All winter she knits between turns. She promised to change colors every time I put her in check. By March my favorite section was a very short purple stripe.

mbm-1887.quote: I crocheted a little basket of berries for a shop window. One strawberry unzips into a coin purse. The owner keeps her bus fare inside and I check for it every time I pass.

mbm-1888.clue: I let my cousin name the colors.
mbm-1888.quote: The yarn shop called it rose. My cousin called it the last spoonful of jam. Guess which name I used when I gave her the scarf.

mbm-1889.clue: My canoe has one perfectly dry corner.
mbm-1889.quote: We lashed a little tin under the bow seat for postcards. At every landing we draw something we saw and slip it in. I could paddle last summer just by shuffling the cards.

mbm-1890.clue: I traded the summit for an afternoon.
mbm-1890.quote: Halfway up the hill, a patch of tiny white flowers opened in the sun. We sat on our packs and watched. The mountain stayed exactly where it was for next Saturday.

mbm-1891.clue: One patch of marble came home in my sketchbook.
mbm-1891.quote: The palace floor had a patch the size of my shoe repaired with dark marble. The guide knew who had laid it. I wrote the mason's name under my sketch and forgot the king's.

mbm-1892.clue: My quilt is one stripe wider on Tuesdays.
mbm-1892.quote: I quilt in a café where a man plays accordion on Tuesdays. I always mean to leave after the second seam. Then he starts another waltz and I find another strip in my bag.

mbm-1893.clue: See that blank window behind the flowered curtain?
mbm-1893.quote: I made a house quilt with windows for family photos. I left one empty until my sister's puppy sat still. It took three weeks and an entire biscuit.

mbm-1894.clue: I made the pompom on the wrong train.
mbm-1894.quote: I was making a blue crochet hat on the platform and took the train in the wrong direction. I had a whole extra hour to make it a splendid pompom. My brother wears my missed stop right on top of his head.

mbm-1895.clue: I copied the handle, not the sword.
mbm-1895.quote: In the museum case was a very grand silver sword with one dull patch where somebody's thumb had rested. I sketched that patch. It was the first time I'd pictured the owner as a person.

mbm-1896.clue: My model planet has a very familiar ring.
mbm-1896.quote: The plastic ring round the milk cap fit my little space station perfectly. I painted it copper and added a docking light. Mum has saved every milk ring since.

mbm-1897.clue: I keep my first belt wrapped around a photograph.
mbm-1897.quote: After practice our class put our shoes on backward for the group picture, just to make the instructor laugh. He holds it right side up in his office. The shoes still look wrong.

mbm-1898.clue: I came home with one pin and no score.
mbm-1898.quote: The alley retired a chipped pin on my birthday. All my friends drew pictures on its side. When I turn it slowly you can see our worst game getting funnier from every angle.

mbm-1899.clue: I save the slow level for my friend.
mbm-1899.quote: Our old racing game has a level with a turtle in the road. My friend refuses to pass until it reaches the grass. We have the slowest finishing time and a spotless turtle record.

mbm-1900.clue: I danced with the girl on the porch.
mbm-1900.quote: At the procession a girl on a low porch opened a yellow paper fan whenever I spread my pollera. I took two steps her way and we danced a whole little figure together across the railing.
